D006-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—maybe a little less, maybe a little more. Things started shifting at church: I’d be full of energy one week, rewriting sermons at 3 a.m., starting three new Bible studies at once, pacing the pulpit like I had lightning in my veins. Then suddenly, I’d drop everything—mid-sentence, mid-project—chasing a new idea that burned too bright to ignore. I don’t know why, but I keep seeing figures in the sanctuary after hours—people who aren’t there. One looks like a man in an old coat, just standing near the altar. I know he’s not real, but I *see* him.

Words have started tripping in my head—rhyming, spinning. "Grace chases the face in the space"—I don’t know what it means, but it echoes when I pray. I also feel watched. Not spiritually—like someone’s *recording* me. The way a child laughs outside, I wonder if it’s coded for me. My wife says I’ve withdrawn. I don’t feel joy like I used to—not in preaching, not in my family. Sometimes, standing on the balcony, a sudden pull comes—just to jump—not because I want to end it, but the urge *jolts* through me.  

I used to have peace. Now I have voices, visions, and a mind that won’t sit still—even when I’m empty inside.

A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)

    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—things started slowly, but they’re getting harder to ignore. Some days, I feel electric—like my brain’s racing so fast I can’t sit still. I’ll start three different things at once in the salon, rearranging stations, mixing chemicals, texting five clients at once, but nothing gets finished. My hands won’t stop moving, and I can’t focus long enough to cut hair right. Then, out of nowhere, I’ll snap—irritable over tiny things, like if a towel isn’t folded just so. Other times, I’m laughing, almost giddy, but it doesn’t last. It’s like my moods are sliding around on their own.

And then there’s the other stuff. I keep feeling things crawling on my skin, like bugs, but when I look—nothing. I’ve brushed my arms in the middle of a trim, trying to shake it off. I sometimes think… the world feels fake, like it’s all going to vanish. Like none of this matters, and it’s all ending soon. I stopped opening the salon for weeks. Didn’t care. I’d stare at the wall, too heavy to move. I even filled a bottle with pills once—didn’t take them, but… I had it ready.

Talking? It’s hard. My thoughts get tangled. I’ll say things and not know how I got there. My staff look at me like I’m speaking another language. I don’t know what’s worse—the buzzing in my head or the silence after.
D006-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Delusional Disorder
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder

D006-D005_h003.question:

D006-D005_h004.question:

I don’t know what’s real anymore. But I can’t perform. I can’t function. And I don’t know how long this has been going on—time blurs.

D006-D005_h006.question:

I know people think I’m losing it. But I’m not sick—just tuned in. The truth is right there, if only they’d listen.

D006-D005_h007.question:

D006-D005_h008.question:

D006-D005_h011.question:

I know people might say that’s not real, but I *know* she’s trying to reach me.

My wife’s worried. Says I’ve changed. I just feel more alive, more aware. Like I’m seeing the world the way it really is.

D006-D005_h021.question:

D006-D005_h025.question:
